# Waypoint

> A shared graph of nodes joined by links from a source to a destination. Humans edit it in the web UI; agents use the HTTP API below. Machine-readable spec: /openapi.json

## Auth

A graph has three keys: `wp_owner_...` (can also set the title), `wp_editor_...` (read and change), `wp_viewer_...` (read only). The viewer key is also the graph ID. Send the key as a bearer token:

    Authorization: Bearer wp_editor_...

or, if you cannot set headers, as `?key=wp_editor_...` on any request (URLs get logged, so prefer the header). Wrong key and unknown graph both give 401.

Find the graph ID from your key:

    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://waypoint.qdat.net/api/session
    # {"role":"editor","graph":"wp_viewer_...","exists":true,"keys":{...}}

A new key set: `curl -X POST https://waypoint.qdat.net/api/graphs`. A graph exists once an editor first writes to it. The reply holds the owner, editor and viewer keys; they cannot be recovered later, so keep them. Name the graph with `PUT /api/graphs/{graph}/title` (owner key). Over MCP, the `create_graph` tool does all of this and opens the new graph.

## Read (viewer key or better)

- GET /api/graphs/{graph}                          summary: title, node/link/conflict counts
- GET /api/graphs/{graph}/nodes?q=text&limit=50    search by title or key ("#12")
- GET /api/graphs/{graph}/nodes/{node}             one node with its links and note
- GET /api/graphs/{graph}/nodes/{node}/neighbours?direction=both|destinations|sources&depth=1
- GET /api/graphs/{graph}/conflicts                links set aside because they join a node to itself
- GET /api/graphs/{graph}/types                    node types, edge types, background colour
- GET /api/graphs/{graph}/full                     whole graph as JSON: nodes (with note, position), links, conflicts
- GET /api/graphs/{graph}/dot                      Graphviz DOT text
- GET /api/graphs/{graph}/positions                absolute node positions
- GET /api/graphs/{graph}/log                      who changed what, oldest first

A node reference is its key (`#12` or `12`), its UUID, or `$N` for the node created by op N (0-based) earlier in the same batch.

## Write (editor key or better)

POST /api/graphs/{graph}/apply takes a batch of ops, applied atomically (any failure changes nothing and the error names `op_index`). Optional headers: `X-Waypoint-Peer: id` is your id for this session (any string you keep; it keys your undo history; use a random one) and `X-Waypoint-Actor: name` is what you call yourself in the change log. Names may repeat and prove nothing; peers are told apart by id. Without an id you are known by your name.

    curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"label":"add task","ops":[{"op":"create_node","title":"Write tests","destinations":["#3"]}]}' \
      https://waypoint.qdat.net/api/graphs/$GRAPH/apply
    # {"results":[{...,"key":13}]}

Ops (field `op`):
- create_node {title, destinations?: [ref], sources?: [ref], x?, y?, node_type?: name}
                                  A batch with 3 or more create_node ops that give no x/y is laid out as a
                                  whole (layers left to right, destinations first, few crossings), below anything
                                  already in the graph. You do not need to pass positions to build a graph.
- rename_node {node, title}
- delete_node {node}              links through it are joined
- link {from, to, edge_type?: name}  from (source) links to to (destination); cycles are fine, a link to itself is refused; relinking retypes
- unlink {from, to}
- move_node {node, x, y, with_destinations?}   with_destinations also moves what hangs off it: with the node taken out, every piece of the graph but the largest moves along (all of it if none is clearly largest; a node that splits nothing takes what it links to)
- set_node_type {node, node_type}       "default" restores the default
- upsert_node_type {name, new_name?, shape?, bg?, fg?, border?, border_width?, corners?}
- upsert_edge_type {name, new_name?, label?, color?, text_color?, width?, line_style?, start?, end?}
- layout {positions: [{node, x, y}, ...]}   sets every node's top-left position at once (all live nodes must be listed)
- tidy {aspect?}   lays out the whole graph afresh (every position is overwritten; aspect = width/height, default 16/9)
- remove_node_type {name}, remove_edge_type {name}
- upsert_tag {name, new_name?, glyph?, color?}   a tag is a coloured one-glyph symbol (an emoji or symbol; `glyph` is required to create one)
- remove_tag {name}
- set_tags {node | from+to, add?: [tag name], remove?: [tag name]}   put tags on a node, or on the link from -> to
- set_note {node, body}           replace the note
- append_note {node, text}        safer when others are editing

## Types and colours

Nodes and edges have a type (a name; the default node type is `default`, the default edge type `link`; the old name `depends_on` still works). `get_types`/`GET /types` lists them with styles. Only the fields you give change. Colours are `#rrggbb`.
- Node type: shape (rect, pill, ellipse, hexagon, rhombus), corners (round, square; for rect, hexagon and rhombus), bg + fg (fill and title; give both; contrast >= 4.5:1), border, border_width (0-10); borders are solid.
- Edge type: color (the line; contrast >= 3:1 with the graph background), text_color (the label; >= 4.5:1), width (1-10), line_style, start and end (none, arrow, dot, bar; `end` is at the destination).
- Out-of-range widths are clamped; bad colours, pairs or shapes fail the op (422) and say why.
- Tags (`todo`, `done`, `assigned-seb`...): defined in the same registry area (`get_types` lists `tags`), referenced by id in the document. Nodes and links can carry several; `get_node`/`get_full_graph` list tag names.
- PUT /api/graphs/{graph}/background {color}   owner key only; edge types that would stop being readable on it are recoloured black or white and listed in the reply.

- POST /api/graphs/{graph}/undo and /redo   undo or redo your own latest batch, as identified by your peer id (409 if none)
- PUT /api/graphs/{graph}/title {title}     owner key only

## Errors

JSON `{"error": "...", "docs": "/llms.txt"}`. 401 missing or wrong key, 403 key role too low, 422 an op failed.
